## Patent Filing Steps in India: Forms and Fees

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/patent-filing-procedure-in-india-step-by-step-guide/

Updated 27 November 202614 minute readBy Sanath V Madgula, reviewed by Praneetha K Rasbag
To file a patent in India, file Form 1 and a specification on the IP India portal. Then request examination within 31 months, answer the examination report and pay renewals after grant. Most avoidable losses happen before the first form is filed, when an invention is disclosed too early or described too thinly.
This guide follows an Indian patent application from the first invention discussion to grant and the years after grant. It reflects the Patents Act, 1970 and the Patents Rules, 2003 as amended by the Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024, which took effect on 15 March 2024. Forms and official fees change from time to time, so each step should be checked against the current IP India material at the time of filing.

### How to file a patent in India: the short answer

- Keep the invention confidential and check that it is patentable.

- Run a prior-art search to see what is genuinely new.

- Draft a provisional or complete specification in Form 2.

- File online on the IP India portal with Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, Form 5 and the official fee.

- Request examination in Form 18 within 31 months of the priority date. The application is published at 18 months, or earlier with Form 9.

- Answer the First Examination Report within six months, attend a hearing if one is offered, and pay renewal fees after grant.

#### Forms, deadlines and official fees at a glance

Official e-filing fees from the First Schedule to the Patents Rules, 2003. The lower rate applies to individuals, startups, small entities and educational institutions. Fees are for a specification of up to 30 pages and 10 claims; extra pages and claims cost more. Professional fees are separate.
| | Step | Form | Deadline | Lower rate | Higher rate
| Provisional or complete application | Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, Form 5 (Form 28 for the lower fee) | Any time before public disclosure. Complete specification within 12 months of a provisional | ₹1,600 | ₹8,000
| Early publication (optional) | Form 9 | Any time after filing | ₹2,500 | ₹12,500
| Request for examination | Form 18 | Within 31 months of the priority date | ₹4,000 | ₹20,000
| Expedited examination (eligible applicants only) | Form 18A | Instead of Form 18 | ₹8,000 | ₹60,000
| Response to the First Examination Report | Reply, with amended claims if needed | Within 6 months, extendable by 3 months | No official fee for the reply itself | No official fee for the reply itself
| Renewal after grant | Renewal fee | Each year from the 3rd year | From ₹800 a year | From ₹4,000 a year

Our patent filing cost guide compares these fees with the USPTO and the EPO.

### Before filing. Is the invention patentable?

An invention must be new, involve an inventive step and be capable of industrial application. These requirements come from section 2(1)(j) of the Act. Section 3 then lists subject matter that is not an invention at all. It includes a mathematical or business method, a computer programme per se and an algorithm under section 3(k), a mere new form of a known substance without enhanced efficacy under section 3(d), and methods of medical treatment under section 3(i).
Software and AI inventions are not excluded as a class. The question is whether the claims define a technical solution to a technical problem rather than a program or method in the abstract. The way the specification explains the technical effect often decides the outcome.
Keep the invention confidential until an application is on file. Section 31 gives only a narrow grace period for specified disclosures, such as display at an exhibition notified by the Government or a paper read before a learned society. A product launch, investor pitch or conference talk outside those categories can destroy novelty in India and in many other countries.

### Step 1. Search the prior art

A patentability search tests the invention against earlier patents and publications before money is spent on drafting. It also shows which features are genuinely new, which helps the drafter place the claims correctly. A search cannot find unpublished applications, so it reduces risk rather than removing it.

### Step 2. Choose the filing route

The route depends on how ready the invention is and where protection is needed.

- Provisional application. A provisional specification secures a filing date for an invention that is still developing. The complete specification must follow within 12 months under section 9(1). If it does not, the application is treated as abandoned.

- Complete application. A complete specification with claims can be filed directly when the invention is fully worked out.

- Convention application. An applicant who first filed in a convention country can file in India within 12 months of that first filing and claim its priority under section 135.

- PCT route. An international application under the Patent Cooperation Treaty keeps options open in many countries. Entry into the Indian national phase is due within 31 months from the priority date.

### Step 3. Draft the specification

The specification is filed in Form 2. A complete specification must describe the invention fully, disclose the best method of performing it known to the applicant and end with claims that define the scope of protection. These requirements appear in section 10. The claims must be clear and must be fairly based on what the description discloses.
Good drafting anticipates examination. The description should support fallback positions, explain the technical advantage and use consistent terminology across the claims, description and drawings. It is very hard to add support later. Amendments under section 59 cannot introduce matter that was not in the application as filed.

### Step 4. File the application

Applications are filed online through the IP India portal at the appropriate patent office. The office is chosen by the applicant's residence or place of business, or by the place where the invention originated. Applicants with no place of business in India use their address for service in India. The Chennai office covers Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry and Lakshadweep. Delhi and Mumbai cover the northern and western states, and Kolkata covers the rest.
Documents usually filed with an Indian patent application
- Form 1, the application itself, with applicant and inventor details.

- Form 2, the provisional or complete specification with drawings and abstract.

- Form 3, the statement and undertaking about corresponding foreign applications under section 8.

- Form 5, the declaration as to inventorship, filed with the complete specification or within the permitted time after it.

- Form 26, the power of attorney, where a patent agent files on the applicant's behalf.

- Proof of right to apply, where the applicant is not the inventor, such as an assignment.

- A certified copy of the priority document for a convention application, where required.

Official fees depend on the applicant. Natural persons, startups, small entities and educational institutions pay reduced fees. Other applicants pay the standard rate. The current schedule is published by IP India.

### Foreign filing permission for inventions made in India

Section 39 restricts residents of India from applying for a patent outside India without written permission from the Patent Office. Permission is not needed where an application for the same invention was filed in India at least six weeks before the foreign filing and no secrecy direction was issued. Permission can be requested in Form 25. Breaching section 39 can lead to the Indian application being treated as abandoned and to penalties, so the first foreign filing should never be made without checking this point.

### Step 5. Publication

An application is ordinarily published in the Patent Office Journal after 18 months from the filing date or the priority date, whichever is earlier. An applicant can request early publication in Form 9. The application is then usually published within one month of the request.
From the date of publication, the applicant has the same privileges and rights as if a patent had been granted on that date. Proceedings for infringement can only begin after grant. This is the effect of section 11A(7), and it is one reason applicants choose early publication.

### Step 6. Request examination

An application is not examined unless the applicant files a request for examination in Form 18. For applications filed on or after 15 March 2024, the request is due within 31 months from the priority date or the filing date, whichever is earlier. The earlier limit was 48 months. An application without a timely request is treated as withdrawn under section 11B.
Expedited examination is available through Form 18A for eligible applicants. The categories include startups, small entities, applicants who chose India as the International Searching Authority or International Preliminary Examining Authority, certain government entities, and applications where at least one natural person applicant is female. Expedited examination moves quickly and leaves little time to prepare responses, so the claims should be ready before it is requested.

### Step 7. Respond to the First Examination Report

The examiner's objections are sent to the applicant in the First Examination Report, usually called the FER. The applicant has six months from the date of the FER to put the application in order for grant. That period can be extended by up to three months on a request in Form 4. If the application is not put in order in time, it is deemed abandoned under section 21.
The 2024 amendments also require an updated Form 3 within three months of the FER, covering foreign applications filed after the Indian application. A careful response addresses every objection, explains the technical distinctions from the cited art and proposes amendments that have clear support in the specification.

### Step 8. Hearing

If objections remain after the written response, the Controller will generally offer a hearing under section 14 before refusing the application. Hearings can be attended by video conference. Written submissions must usually be filed within fifteen days after the hearing. The Controller then decides whether to grant or refuse the application.

### Step 9. Pre grant opposition

Any person may file a representation opposing the grant under section 25(1) after publication and before grant. The grounds include lack of novelty, obviousness, non patentable subject matter and failure to disclose foreign application details. The Rules also bar grant before six months from publication, which gives third parties time to oppose.

### Step 10. Grant and life after grant

Once the Controller is satisfied, the patent is granted and the grant is published in the Journal. The term is 20 years from the date of filing of the application under section 53. For a PCT national phase application, that date is the international filing date.

- Post grant opposition. An interested person may oppose within one year from the date of publication of the grant under section 25(2).

- Renewal fees. Annual renewal fees keep the patent in force. Arrears that fall due before grant must be paid within the time the Rules allow after grant. Paying at least four years in advance electronically attracts a ten per cent reduction.

- Statement of working. The patentee must file Form 27 once for every period of three financial years, starting with the financial year after grant. It is due within six months after the end of each period.

- Records. Assignments must be in writing under section 68. They and licences should be registered with the Patent Office under section 69, because an unregistered document may not be admitted as evidence of title.

### How long does it take?

There is no fixed timetable. Publication follows at 18 months unless it is brought forward. Examination starts only after a request and depends on the backlog in the relevant technology group. Expedited examination can produce a decision far faster than the regular route. The single most controllable factor is the quality of the specification and the response, because every avoidable objection adds a round of correspondence.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Who can file a patent application in India?

Under section 6 of the Patents Act, the person claiming to be the true and first inventor can apply. So can that inventor's assignee, or the legal representative of a deceased inventor. Any of them may apply alone or jointly with others.

#### What are the stages from filing to grant of a patent in India?

Filing, publication at 18 months, a request for examination within 31 months, the First Examination Report and the reply within six months. A hearing may follow. The Controller then grants or refuses the patent, and renewals keep it in force.

#### How much does it cost to file a patent in India?

In official fees, an individual, startup or small entity pays ₹1,600 to file online and ₹4,000 to request examination, so ₹5,600 in total for a specification of up to 30 pages and 10 claims. A large company pays ₹8,000 and ₹20,000. Drafting and attorney fees are separate and usually cost more than the official fees.

#### How long does it take to get a patent in India?

Through the regular route, commonly two to four years from filing, depending on the technology group. Through expedited examination, eligible applicants can sometimes be granted within a year.

#### Can I file a patent application in India myself?

Yes. An applicant can file and prosecute an application in its own name. Only a registered patent agent may practise as an agent before the Patent Office, although advocates may appear at hearings. Most applicants use an agent because drafting and prosecution decisions affect the value of the patent for its whole life. Our guide to choosing an intellectual property lawyer explains how to check an agent's registration.

#### Is a provisional application worth filing?

It is useful when the invention needs a date before it is complete or before a disclosure that cannot be delayed. It is not a shortcut. Features that are not described in the provisional specification do not receive its date.

#### Does an Indian patent protect the invention in other countries?

No. Patents are territorial. Protection abroad needs separate filings, usually through the Paris Convention within 12 months or through the PCT. Check section 39 first if the invention was made in India.

#### What is the difference between patent filing and patent registration?

People often use the words interchangeably. Filing starts the process. A patent is granted only after examination, and the Patent Office then records it in the register of patents.

#### How do I file a patent application online in India?

Applications are filed through the IP India online filing portal. The applicant or patent agent registers on the portal, uploads Forms 1, 2, 3 and 5 with the specification and drawings, signs them with a digital signature certificate and pays the official fee online. The portal issues a filing receipt with the application number and filing date. Paper filing is still possible but costs more.

#### Can I patent an idea in India?

Not an idea on its own. A patent protects an invention described in enough detail for a skilled person to carry it out, which is the sufficiency requirement in section 10. Once you can explain how the idea works, a provisional application can secure a filing date while development continues.

#### How do I patent a product in India?

Patent the technical features that make the product work, such as its structure, mechanism, circuit or manufacturing process, rather than the product name or appearance. The appearance can be protected separately through design registration and the name through a trade mark. File before the product is launched, shown to investors or sold, because public disclosure can destroy novelty.

#### Can I file a patent in India for free?

No. Official fees apply to every application, but natural persons, startups, small entities and educational institutions pay reduced fees. Startups can also request expedited examination at a reduced fee. The government's SIPP scheme, which paid patent agents' fees for startups, lapsed on 31 March 2026 and no replacement has been announced.

### Official sources

- The Patents Act, 1970, published by IP India

- Patents Rules and amendments, published by IP India

- IP India patent forms and official fees

## Patent Cost in India 2026, vs US and Europe

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/patent-filing-cost-india-us-europe/

By Praneetha K RasbagPublished 24 October 2026Updated 23 November 20268 minute read
Filing a patent application in India costs ₹1,600 in official fees online for an individual, startup, small entity or educational institution, and ₹8,000 for any other applicant. A provisional application pays the same ₹1,600 or ₹8,000, and the complete specification filed after it costs nothing extra up to 30 pages and 10 claims. Examination is a separate request costing ₹4,000 or ₹20,000.
These official fees are far lower than in the US or Europe, and the gap is largest for startups and small entities. But official fees are only one part of the budget, and each office charges in a different way.
This guide sets out the main official fees at each office as they stand in October 2026. It does not include attorney fees, drafting, translations or currency conversion. Those usually cost more than the official fees themselves.
Key points
- In India, a startup or small entity can file and request examination online for ₹5,600 in official fees. A large company pays ₹28,000.

- At the USPTO, filing, search, examination and issue fees for a large entity total $3,290. Small entities pay 40 percent and micro entities 20 percent of that.

- At the EPO, the main fees up to grant total about €5,595 from 1 April 2026, before claims fees and renewal fees.

- Renewal fees over the life of a patent usually cost more than getting the patent granted.

- Every office charges extra for long specifications or many claims, so drafting choices affect cost.

### India: official fees under the Patents Rules

The First Schedule to the Patents Rules, 2003 sets the fees. There are two rates. The lower rate applies to a natural person, a startup, a small entity or an educational institution. The higher rate applies to everyone else, including any application where such a person files jointly with a large company. Paper filing costs about 10 percent more than online filing.

#### Filing and examination

- Application for a patent (Form 1): ₹1,600 at the lower rate and ₹8,000 at the higher rate, for online filing.

- The base fee covers up to 30 pages and 10 claims. Each extra sheet costs ₹160 or ₹800. Each claim above 10 costs ₹320 or ₹1,600.

- Request for examination (Form 18): ₹4,000 or ₹20,000. A request made under rule 20(4)(ii) costs ₹5,600 or ₹28,000.

- Request for expedited examination (Form 18A): ₹8,000 or ₹60,000. Expedited examination is open only to specified categories of applicant.

- Request for early publication (Form 9): ₹2,500 or ₹12,500.

So a startup filing a complete specification of 30 pages with 10 claims pays ₹5,600 to file and request examination. A large company pays ₹28,000 for the same application. A startup or small entity claims the lower rate by filing Form 28 with supporting evidence. Foreign companies can qualify as startups or small entities if they meet the definitions in the Rules.

#### Provisional patent cost in India

A provisional application is filed on Form 1 with a provisional specification on Form 2. The official fee is the same as for any application: ₹1,600 online at the lower rate and ₹8,000 at the higher rate. Paper filing costs ₹1,750 or ₹8,800.
The complete specification must follow within 12 months. Under entry 2 of the First Schedule, filing it carries no fee up to 30 pages and 10 claims. Extra sheets and claims are charged at the same rates as above.
So the official cost of a provisional route for a startup is ₹1,600 at filing, then ₹4,000 when examination is requested. Drafting and attorney fees are separate. Our guide on when to file a PCT application explains what to decide before the 12 month deadline.

#### Renewal fees

Renewal fees start in the third year, counted from the date of the patent. They rise in four bands.

- Years 3 to 6: ₹800 or ₹4,000 a year.

- Years 7 to 10: ₹2,400 or ₹12,000 a year.

- Years 11 to 15: ₹4,800 or ₹24,000 a year.

- Years 16 to 20: ₹8,000 or ₹40,000 a year.

Keeping a patent alive for the full 20 years costs ₹76,800 in renewal fees at the lower rate. At the higher rate it costs ₹3,84,000. Our step by step guide to filing a patent in India explains where each fee falls in the process.

### United States: USPTO fees

The USPTO fee schedule effective 19 January 2025 is still current. It has three tiers. Small entities pay 40 percent of the large entity fee. Micro entities pay 20 percent. Small entity status depends mainly on size and on not having licensed the invention to a large entity. Micro entity status adds limits on income and on earlier filings.

- Basic filing fee for a utility application: $350, $140 or $70.

- Search fee: $770, $308 or $154.

- Examination fee: $880, $352 or $176.

- Issue fee on allowance: $1,290, $516 or $258.

- Provisional application: $325, $130 or $65.

- Each claim over 20: $200. Each independent claim over three: $600. Both are at the large entity rate.

- A surcharge of $400 for a large entity applies to applications not filed electronically.

So the core fees from filing to grant total $3,290 for a large entity, $1,316 for a small entity and $658 for a micro entity. After grant, maintenance fees fall due at 3.5, 7.5 and 11.5 years. For a large entity they are $2,150, $4,040 and $8,280. Small and micro entities pay the same reduced percentages.

### Europe: EPO fees from 1 April 2026

The EPO adjusted its fees on 1 April 2026. A European patent application pays the following main fees.

- Filing fee for online filing: €135. Each page above 35 costs €17 more.

- Search fee: €1,595.

- Designation fee: €720, covering all designated states.

- Examination fee: €2,010 for a direct European application. A Euro PCT application without a supplementary search report pays €2,240.

- Fee for grant: €1,135.

- Claims fee: €290 for each claim from the 16th to the 50th, and €720 from the 51st.

These main fees total about €5,595 up to grant. Renewal fees are payable to the EPO while the application is pending. They start in the third year counted from the filing date. The third year fee is €725 and the fee reaches €1,865 from the tenth year.
A 30 percent reduction applies to several fees for microenterprises, natural persons, non profit bodies, universities and public research organisations. The applicant must have filed fewer than five European applications in the previous five years. Small and medium enterprises do not qualify. After grant, the patent is either validated country by country or registered as a Unitary Patent. Each route has its own renewal and translation costs.

### How the three systems compare

- Who gets a discount. India gives the lower rate to individuals, startups, small entities and educational institutions. The discount is often 80 percent. The US gives 60 percent off to small entities and 80 percent off to micro entities. The EPO gives 30 percent off to a narrower group.

- When examination is paid. India charges for examination only when the applicant asks for it, within 31 months from priority. The US charges search and examination fees on filing. They may be paid later with a surcharge. The EPO examination and designation fees fall due within six months after the search report is published.

- Renewals. India and the EPO charge annual fees. The US charges three maintenance fees after grant.

- Size of the application. All three charge for extra pages and claims. India counts sheets above 30 and claims above 10. The EPO counts claims above 15. The US counts claims above 20 and independent claims above three.

For an Indian startup, the official fees for the Indian application are small. The real cost lies in drafting, in responding to examination reports and in filing abroad. Our guide to protecting startup IP on a budget covers how to stage those costs, and our note on when to file a PCT application covers the timing of foreign filings.
At a glance | | Point | India | United States | EPO
| Discount | Often 80% for individuals, startups, small entities and educational institutions | 60% small entity, 80% micro entity | 30% for a narrower group
| Examination fee | Only on request, within 31 months from priority | Due on filing, or later with a surcharge | Within six months after the search report
| Renewals | Annual fees | Three maintenance fees after grant | Annual fees
| Excess fees | Sheets above 30, claims above 10 | Claims above 20, independent claims above three | Claims above 15

### Practical steps to control cost

- Check whether you qualify for the lower rate in India, small or micro entity status in the US, or the EPO reduction. File the required declaration at the start.

- Draft claims with care. In India, keep to 10 claims where you can. At the EPO, keep to 15. In the US, keep to 20 claims and three independent claims.

- Decide early whether expedited examination in India is worth its higher fee for your applicant category.

- Budget for renewal fees before grant. They grow each year and can exceed the cost of filing.

- Review the portfolio each year and drop patents that no longer protect a product or a licence.

Our patent services cover drafting and filing in India, and our international filing support covers the US, the EPO and PCT routes.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How much does a provisional patent cost in India?

The official fee is ₹1,600 online for an individual, startup or small entity and ₹8,000 for others. Filing the complete specification later costs nothing extra up to 30 pages and 10 claims.

#### What is the patent filing cost in India for a startup?

The official fees to file online and request examination are ₹5,600 for a complete specification up to 30 pages and 10 claims. Attorney and drafting fees are extra.

#### How much does a US patent cost in official fees?

Filing, search, examination and issue fees total $3,290 for a large entity, $1,316 for a small entity and $658 for a micro entity. Extra claims and maintenance fees cost more.

#### How much are EPO fees in 2026?

From 1 April 2026 the main fees are €135 to file online, €1,595 for search, €720 for designation, €2,010 for examination and €1,135 for grant.

## Provisional patent application: India, US, Europe

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/provisional-patent-application-india-us-europe/

By Sanath V MadgulaPublished 7 November 20268 minute read
What does a provisional patent application actually protect? It fixes a filing date for what it describes, and nothing more. India and the US both offer a provisional application with a 12 month life. The EPO and the UK IPO have no separate provisional form, but an early filing there works in much the same way.
The value of any first filing depends on one question. Does the later application claim something the first filing clearly described? If it does, the claim keeps the early date. If it does not, the claim falls back to the later date, and anything published in between can be cited against it.
Key points
- In India, a complete specification must follow a provisional within 12 months. Otherwise section 9(1) of the Patents Act, 1970 deems the application abandoned.

- In the US, a provisional needs no claims and lapses 12 months after filing under 35 U.S.C. § 111(b). The later application must normally be filed within that period. A petition can extend it by two months for unintentional delay.

- The EPO has no provisional form. It accepts a US or Indian provisional as a priority filing, and an EPO filing without claims still receives a date.

- In every system, a claim keeps the early date only if the first filing supports it. A short provisional rarely supports the claims that matter.

- Indian residents need a foreign filing permit, or an Indian filing made at least six weeks earlier, before filing a first application abroad.

### What a provisional application is

A provisional application is a first filing that describes the invention without claims or the other formal parts. It is not examined. Its only job is to fix a date. Within 12 months the applicant files the full application, which is examined and granted. The provisional then matters only as evidence of what was described, and when.

### India: provisional and complete specifications

Section 9(1) of the Patents Act, 1970 requires a complete specification within 12 months of a provisional one. If it is not filed in time, the application is deemed to be abandoned. Section 10(1) says every specification, provisional or complete, must describe the invention and carry a title. The requirement for claims and an abstract in section 10(4) applies only to the complete specification.
The priority date of each claim is decided under section 11. A claim in the complete specification that is fairly based on the matter disclosed in the provisional gets the provisional filing date. A claim that is not fairly based on it gets the date of the complete specification.
Under section 9(2), several related provisionals by one applicant may be covered by one complete specification, with the 12 months running from the earliest. Under section 9(4), the Controller may cancel the provisional on request before grant and postdate the application to the complete specification.
The Indian provisional route is for national first filings only. Section 9(1) excludes convention applications and PCT national phase applications. The official fee is the same Form 1 fee as any application. Our step by step guide to filing a patent in India sets out the forms, fees and later deadlines.

### United States: the provisional application under section 111(b)

Under 35 U.S.C. § 111(b), a provisional must contain a specification meeting section 112(a) and any drawings required by section 113. Claims are not required. The filing date is the date the specification is received. The application is abandoned 12 months after filing and cannot be revived after that period.
Section 119(e)(1) gives a later nonprovisional or PCT application the benefit of the provisional date. Three conditions apply. The later application must be filed within 12 months. It must name an inventor in common and refer specifically to the provisional. The provisional must describe the claimed invention in the manner section 112(a) requires, except for best mode. The statute lets the USPTO extend the 12 months by two more months where the delay was unintentional.
The official fee is low. The current USPTO filing fee for a provisional is $325, $130 or $65, by entity size. A size fee applies above 100 sheets.
The early date is not presumed. In Dynamic Drinkware v National Graphics (Fed. Cir. 4 September 2015, No. 2015‑1214), the court refused to presume that a prior art patent was entitled to its provisional date. The petitioner relying on that date had to prove that the provisional supported the claims. Support is therefore tested only when it matters, often in litigation or an inter partes review.

### Europe: no provisional, but an early first filing works

The European Patent Convention has no provisional application. Under Article 87(1) EPC, a filing in a Paris Convention state or WTO member gives 12 months of priority for the same invention. Under Article 87(3), any filing that establishes a filing date counts, whatever later happens to it. A 1996 notice of the EPO President (OJ EPO 1996, 81) confirms that a US provisional gives a right of priority.
The EPO can itself act as the first filing office. Under Rule 40(1) EPC, a filing date needs only a request for a patent, applicant details and a description. Claims can follow later under Rule 58. An applicant can therefore file a description at the EPO and use it as a priority basis within 12 months.
The priority test is strict. The EPO Guidelines apply the test from G 2/98. The claimed subject matter must be directly and unambiguously derivable from the priority document as a whole. A broad statement of the idea will not carry a narrower claim that adds a feature described only later.
Ownership also matters. In G 1/22 and G 2/22 of 10 October 2023, the Enlarged Board held that the EPO may assess entitlement to priority. It held that an applicant who claims priority correctly is presumed to be entitled to it, and the presumption is rebuttable. This helps where a US provisional was filed in the inventors' names and the later application in the company's name. Clear assignments remain the safer course.

### United Kingdom

The UK IPO also has no provisional form. Under section 15(1) of the Patents Act 1977, a filing date needs a request, applicant details and a description. Claims and the abstract must follow within the prescribed period under section 15(10). Under section 5(2), an invention supported by matter disclosed in an earlier application filed in the previous 12 months takes that earlier date. A late declaration can be allowed where the failure to file within 12 months was unintentional.

### Where the routes differ

- Name and form. India and the US have a named provisional application. The EPO and the UK use an ordinary first filing without claims.

- Support standard. India asks whether a claim is fairly based on the provisional. The US asks whether the provisional meets the written description and enablement requirements of section 112(a). The EPO asks whether the claim is directly and unambiguously derivable. The UK asks whether the invention is supported by matter disclosed. The EPO test is usually the hardest to meet.

- Late filing. The US statute allows two extra months for unintentional delay. The EPO can restore the priority period if all due care was taken. The request and the European filing must both follow within two months. Section 9(1) of the Indian Act states the 12 months as a fixed period with deemed abandonment.

- Where to file first. Section 39 of the Indian Act bars an Indian resident from filing abroad without a written permit. The exception is an Indian application filed at least six weeks earlier with no secrecy direction in force.

### Practical steps

- Write the provisional as if it were the complete. Describe every embodiment, alternative and parameter range you may later want to claim. Include working examples and drawings. Add draft claims even where they are optional, because they show what you regarded as the invention.

- File again before each disclosure. If the design changes before a launch, a pitch or a paper, file a further provisional. In India, section 9(2) allows related provisionals to be covered by one complete specification.

- Keep the ownership chain clean. Take written assignments from inventors before the first filing. Name the same applicant in later filings where possible.

- Plan the foreign route before you file. Indian residents should file first in India or obtain a section 39 permit. Use the 12 month window to decide on a PCT application or direct national filings. Our note on when to file a PCT application covers that choice.

- Diarise 12 months from the first filing. A later provisional does not restart the period for matter already disclosed.

For foreign applicants filing in India, see our guide to India patent filing for foreign applicants. For official fees in each office, see our patent filing cost comparison.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How long is a provisional patent application valid?

Twelve months in both India and the US. In India the complete specification must be filed within that period. In the US the later application must be filed within 12 months to claim the provisional date.

#### Can a US provisional application be used to claim priority in India or Europe?

Yes. A US provisional fixes a filing date, so a later Indian or European application can claim its priority within 12 months. Each claim keeps that date only if the provisional supports it.

#### Does a provisional patent application need claims?

No. Neither Indian nor US law requires claims in a provisional. Claims are required in the complete or nonprovisional application. Including draft claims in the provisional is still good practice.

### Official source

- The Patents Act, 1970, section 11 (IP India)

- 35 U.S.C. § 111 and 35 U.S.C. § 119

- USPTO fee schedule

- Article 87 EPC and EPO Guidelines A‑II, 4.1 (date of filing)

- Notice of the EPO President on US provisional applications, OJ EPO 1996, 81

## India Patent Filing for US and European Companies

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/india-patent-filing-for-foreign-applicants/

India national phaseParis ConventionProsecution and compliance
India is one of the largest markets and manufacturing bases for technology, pharmaceuticals and consumer products. For US and European companies, an Indian patent is often the right that matters most when products are made, sold or copied here.
PRASA IP works with in house patent teams, foreign patent firms and founders who need patents in India. We handle Indian filing, prosecution and reporting through registered Indian patent agents and IP attorneys, and we report in the format that US and European teams expect. This page explains how a foreign applicant enters India and where Indian practice differs from USPTO and EPO practice.

### Two routes into India

#### PCT national phase

Most foreign applicants reach India through the Patent Cooperation Treaty. The Indian national phase must be entered within 31 months from the priority date. Treat this as a fixed deadline. Relief after a missed national phase date is limited and uncertain, so the docket should carry an early internal reminder.

#### Paris Convention application

An applicant that first filed in the United States, at the EPO or in a European national office can file directly in India within 12 months and claim that priority. A US provisional application can serve as the priority filing. This route suits applicants who need an Indian application quickly or who did not file a PCT application.

### What we need to enter India

Documents and information for an Indian filing
- The application as published, or the claims you want to pursue, in English.

- Applicant and inventor names, addresses and nationalities.

- A power of attorney in favour of the Indian patent agent, in Form 26.

- Proof of the applicant's right to apply, such as an assignment from the inventors, where the applicant is a company.

- A certified copy of the priority document for a Paris Convention filing, where it is not available to the Patent Office electronically.

- Details of corresponding applications in other countries for Form 3.

- An address for service in India, which is normally the agent's address.

Official fees are calculated on the number of pages and claims, with additional fees above 30 pages and 10 claims. A preliminary amendment before entry can reduce cost and bring the claims into a form that suits Indian law. Companies that meet the definition of a startup or small entity in the Rules, including qualifying foreign entities, pay reduced fees.

#### Official fees for a foreign company

Indian official fees are low by US and European standards. The table shows e-filing fees from the First Schedule to the Patents Rules. Approximate US dollar amounts use ₹88 to US$1 and are rounded.
| | Item | Large entity | Startup or small entity
| Application (Form 1) | ₹8,000 (about US$90) | ₹1,600 (about US$18)
| Each page above 30 | ₹800 | ₹160
| Each claim above 10 | ₹1,600 | ₹320
| Request for examination (Form 18) | ₹20,000 (about US$230) | ₹4,000 (about US$45)
| Expedited examination (Form 18A) | ₹60,000 (about US$680) | ₹8,000 (about US$90)
| Permission to file abroad (Form 25) | ₹8,000 | ₹1,600
| Power of attorney (Form 26) | No fee | No fee
| Annual renewal, years 3 to 6 | ₹4,000 a year | ₹800 a year

Startup and small entity rates are also available to qualifying foreign companies with suitable evidence. Professional fees for drafting, prosecution and hearings are separate; see our comparison of patent costs in India, the US and Europe.

### Inventors in India: the foreign filing licence

Many US and European companies run R&D teams in India. If any inventor is resident in India, section 39 of the Patents Act applies before anything is filed abroad, including a US provisional, an EP application or a PCT application.

- Option 1: file in India first. File an Indian application, wait six weeks, and file abroad if no secrecy direction has issued in that time.

- Option 2: ask for permission. File Form 25 with the Indian Patent Office and file abroad once written permission is granted. The Controller is required to dispose of the request within 21 days, and requests are normally dealt with faster.

- Defence and atomic energy inventions need the prior consent of the Central Government, which takes longer.

The consequences of getting this wrong are serious. An Indian application filed in breach of section 39 is treated as abandoned, a granted Indian patent can be revoked under section 64(1)(n), and section 118 provides for a fine, imprisonment of up to two years, or both. The Delhi High Court confirmed in Puneet Kaushik v Union of India that a PCT application filed directly as a first filing still needs permission.
If the invention was also made partly in the United States, a USPTO foreign filing licence under 35 U.S.C. section 184 may be needed as well. Joint US and Indian inventor teams should agree the first filing country and the licences before anyone files. We regularly obtain Form 25 permissions for foreign companies with Indian inventors.

### Request examination at entry

For applications filed on or after 15 March 2024, the request for examination is due within 31 months from the priority date. That is the same date as the PCT national phase deadline. In practice, most national phase applications therefore request examination when they enter India. Older PCT applications with an international filing date before 15 March 2024 had a 48 month limit.

### Where Indian practice differs from US and European practice

#### Section 3 exclusions

Section 3(k) excludes mathematical and business methods, computer programmes per se and algorithms. Claims that pass in the United States can fail here if they read as software in the abstract. The Patent Office and the Delhi High Court look for a technical effect or technical contribution, which is closer to EPO reasoning than to US subject matter eligibility law. Section 3(d) restricts claims to new forms of known substances unless they show enhanced efficacy. Section 3(i) excludes methods of treatment of humans and animals, so US method of treatment claims usually need to be recast.

#### Section 8 disclosure of foreign applications

India requires applicants to disclose corresponding foreign applications in Form 3 and to keep that information current. Under the 2024 amendments, an updated statement is due within three months of the First Examination Report. The Controller can also require details of foreign search and examination. Failure to comply is a ground for opposition and revocation, so we track every family member and update Form 3 at the right time.

#### Claim amendments

Section 59 allows amendments only by way of disclaimer, correction, explanation or incorporation of actual fact. The amended matter must be disclosed in substance in the specification, and amended claims must fall within the scope of the existing claims. Courts have taken a more liberal view of that second condition before grant, but examiners still apply section 59 closely. Claims copied from a granted US or EP patent are a useful starting point, but they still need to be checked against the Indian specification and Indian objections.

### Prosecution timeline in India

- Examination. The First Examination Report sets out objections. The applicant has six months to respond, extendable by up to three months.

- Hearing. If objections remain, the Controller generally offers a hearing, which can be held by video conference. Written submissions follow within fifteen days.

- Opposition. Third parties can file a pre grant opposition after publication. Grant cannot occur until six months after publication.

- Grant and term. The patent lasts 20 years from the international filing date for a PCT national phase application, or from the Indian filing date for a direct filing.

### After grant

Foreign patentees carry the same duties as Indian ones. Annual renewal fees keep the patent in force. A statement of working in Form 27 is due once for every period of three financial years, within six months after the period ends. Section 146 allows the Controller to ask for further information about commercial working. Missing these obligations can weaken the patent in licensing or enforcement.
Patent disputes in India are heard by the High Courts and district courts under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015. The Delhi High Court has had a dedicated Intellectual Property Division since 2021, and the Madras High Court set up one in 2023. Both have developed a substantial body of patent case law, including on standard essential patents.

### How we work with US and European teams

- Instructions accepted from in house counsel, foreign patent firms and founders.

- Reporting in English with clear recommendations, deadlines and cost estimates for each action.

- Responses prepared by professionals with engineering and legal training, who understand US and EPO prosecution histories and can use them in India.

- Docketing of Indian deadlines alongside the rest of the family, including Form 3 and Form 27.

Indian companies filing abroad can read about our US, EP and PCT patent support. For the Indian procedure from first filing to grant, see our step by step guide to patent filing in India.

### Common mistakes foreign applicants make in India

- Treating the 31 month deadline as flexible. Relief for a missed national phase entry is narrow. Docket it with an internal reminder at month 28.

- Forgetting the request for examination. For applications filed on or after 15 March 2024 it is due at 31 months, the same day as national phase entry. A missed request means the application is treated as withdrawn.

- Late or incomplete Form 3. Section 8 disclosures of foreign applications must be kept current. Gaps are a ground for opposition and revocation years later.

- Not filing the original power of attorney or assignment in time. Keep signed originals ready before entry.

- Entering with US method of treatment or software claims unchanged. Sections 3(i) and 3(k) will lead to objections. A preliminary amendment at entry saves a round of examination.

- Filing abroad first when an inventor lives in India. Section 39 applies even if the applicant is a foreign company.

- Missing Form 27. The statement of working is due once every three financial years after grant.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Can a US or European company file a patent in India without an Indian agent?

A foreign applicant must give an address for service in India. In practice, foreign companies appoint a registered Indian patent agent, who files and prosecutes the application and receives official correspondence.

#### Is the 31 month national phase deadline extendable?

It should be treated as fixed. Some relief provisions exist, but they are narrow and their outcome is uncertain.

#### Can we use our granted US or EP claims in India?

Often, with adjustments. The claims must be supported by the Indian specification, must avoid section 3 exclusions and must meet the limits on amendment in section 59.

#### Our company is in the US but one inventor lives in India. Do we need Indian permission?

Yes. Section 39 depends on the inventor being resident in India, not on where the applicant company is based. File in India first and wait six weeks, or obtain written permission in Form 25 before filing abroad.

#### Do we need to file Form 27 every year?

No. Since the 2024 amendments, Form 27 is filed once for every period of three financial years after grant.

### Official sources

- The Patents Act, 1970, published by IP India

- Patents Rules and amendments, published by IP India

- IP India patent forms and official fees

- WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty resources

- IP India: patent forms and official fees

- The Patents Act, 1970, section 39

- Patent filing cost in India, the US and Europe

## When to File a PCT Application: Cost and Timing

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/when-to-file-pct-application/

By Sanath V MadgulaPublished 29 September 202610 minute read
A PCT application is not a world patent. It is a way to buy time and a first opinion on patentability before committing to expensive national filings. Whether it saves money depends on how many countries you need and how quickly you need a grant.
The Patent Cooperation Treaty lets an applicant file one international application that has effect in more than 150 contracting states. The applicant receives an international search report and a written opinion, then decides later which countries to enter. Those benefits are real. So are the extra fees and the extra time. This article explains when the PCT route earns its cost and when a direct filing is the better choice.

### How the PCT timeline works

- Month 0. The first application sets the priority date. It might be a US or Indian provisional application, a first filing at the EPO, or a national filing such as one at the UK IPO.

- Month 12. The PCT application must be filed to claim that priority. Direct filings under the Paris Convention share the same 12 month limit.

- About month 16. The International Searching Authority usually issues the international search report and written opinion by this point. The applicant can amend the claims under Article 19 within two months of the report or by month 16, whichever is later.

- Month 18. WIPO publishes the application.

- Month 22. The usual last date to demand international preliminary examination under Chapter II, which allows argument and amendment before an examiner.

- Month 30 or 31. National phase entry. Most countries, including the United States, China and Japan, apply 30 months from priority. India and the EPO allow 31 months. China accepts entry up to 32 months on payment of a surcharge.

### When a PCT application makes sense

A useful rule of thumb is to consider the PCT when protection may be needed in more than three countries, or when the countries are not yet known. For a small number of certain markets, direct filings are often cheaper and faster. The PCT usually earns its cost in these situations.

- Many markets. One filing preserves rights everywhere for up to 30 or 31 months. National fees, translations and local attorney costs are deferred until the business knows where it sells.

- Uncertain markets or funding. A startup that expects to raise money or find a licensee can postpone the largest costs by about 18 months.

- A useful search early. The search report and written opinion show the strength of the claims before national spending begins. A negative opinion is cheap information. It can justify narrowing the claims or dropping the application before costs multiply.

- Faster examination later. A positive written opinion or preliminary examination report can support accelerated examination in many offices through the PCT Patent Prosecution Highway.

### When a PCT application wastes money

If the applicant will only ever file in one or two countries, the PCT adds international fees and roughly 18 months of delay before national examination begins. The patent term does not pause for that delay. In India, the United States and Europe, the term generally runs 20 years from the filing date of the application, which for a PCT national phase is the international filing date. By the time a PCT application enters the national phase, about a year and a half of the term has already run. If examination then takes several years, the granted patent may have well under 15 years left. The United States partly compensates for office delays through patent term adjustment, but India and Europe do not.
For one or two known markets, filing directly in those countries within the 12 month priority year usually gives a quicker grant and lower total cost. The same logic applies when a fast grant matters commercially, for example to enforce against an early copier.

### Choose the International Searching Authority deliberately

The receiving office decides which International Searching Authorities are available. Applicants filing in Europe normally receive an EPO search. US applicants filing at the USPTO can choose among several authorities, and many choose the USPTO, the EPO or the Korean office depending on cost and target markets. Applicants filing at the Indian Patent Office can choose the Indian Patent Office, the EPO, the USPTO, the Japan Patent Office, the Swedish, Austrian and Australian offices or CNIPA. The choice affects cost and later strategy.

- Indian Patent Office. The search fee is much lower, with a further reduction for eligible applicants. Choosing India as ISA or IPEA is also a ground for expedited examination in the Indian national phase.

- EPO. The search fee is higher. If the application later enters the European phase, the EPO does not run a supplementary European search, which saves that fee and time. An EPO opinion is also widely accepted for PCT PPH requests.

- Other authorities. The best choice often follows the most important market, because a positive opinion from a partner office is most useful where that office has a PPH arrangement.

### Using a positive search to cut prosecution cost

#### United States

The USPTO accepts PCT PPH requests based on a positive written opinion or preliminary examination report from partner authorities. Track One prioritized examination is not available when a PCT application enters the US national stage under 35 U.S.C. section 371. It becomes available only later, with a request for continued examination. An applicant who wants Track One from the start can instead file a bypass continuation of the PCT application under section 111(a).

#### Europe

When the EPO was the search authority, the European phase can move quickly because no new search is needed. The applicant can also request accelerated prosecution under PACE without an official fee, or use a PPH request based on work from a partner office. After grant, choosing a Unitary Patent gives one renewal fee for the 18 participating EU states, while countries such as the UK, Spain and Poland still need a national European patent and national renewal fees.

#### PCT Patent Prosecution Highway in general

Under PCT PPH programmes, an applicant whose claims were found novel, inventive and industrially applicable in the written opinion or preliminary examination report can ask participating national offices to accelerate examination. The national claims must correspond to the claims found allowable. Offices such as the USPTO, the EPO, the JPO, KIPO and CNIPA take part in PPH networks, although the partner offices and conditions differ. The result is usually fewer office actions and lower attorney costs.

#### India

India is not a member of the Global PPH. Its PPH arrangement with the Japan Patent Office was launched in December 2019 as a three year pilot, with limits on technology fields and annual numbers. Check with IP India whether it is still accepting requests before relying on it. For Indian national phase applications, the practical fast route is expedited examination in Form 18A. Eligible grounds include choosing India as ISA or IPEA and startup status.

#### South East Asia

The ASEAN Patent Examination Co-operation, known as ASPEC, lets applicants in Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam use the search and examination results of one participating office to support examination in another. A PCT version accepts a written opinion or preliminary examination report prepared by an ASEAN authority, which currently means Singapore or the Philippines. ASPEC+, launched in April 2026, lets several participating offices work on the same application together with committed timelines for the first office action.

### Cost savers inside the PCT route

- Use Article 19 or Chapter II amendments to fix claims once, before they are copied into many national applications.

- Natural persons who are nationals and residents of India qualify for a 90 per cent reduction in certain PCT fees. Companies do not.

- Check foreign filing licence rules in the country where the invention was made. For inventions made in the United States, 35 U.S.C. section 184 requires a foreign filing licence before filing abroad within six months of a US filing, or before any first filing abroad. The USPTO normally grants it with the filing receipt of a US application. Several European countries have their own rules. The UK restricts first filings abroad for certain sensitive inventions. France requires European and PCT applications by French applicants to be filed through INPI unless they claim a French priority. Germany restricts inventions that contain state secrets.

- In India, section 39 of the Patents Act applies. If the PCT claims priority from an Indian application, file it only after six weeks have passed with no secrecy direction. If the PCT is the first filing, even at the Indian Patent Office as receiving office, obtain written permission in Form 25 first. The Delhi High Court confirmed this in Puneet Kaushik v Union of India.

- Decide country by country at month 28, not month 30, so translations and local instructions are not rushed.

Foreign applicants entering India from a PCT application can read our page on India patent filing for foreign applicants. Indian companies can read about our US, EP and PCT patent support. Startups watching every rupee should also see our note on protecting IP on a startup budget.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Is a PCT application worth it for only one foreign country?

Usually not. A direct filing in that country within 12 months of the first application is normally cheaper and leads to an earlier grant. The PCT may still help if the applicant needs an early search opinion or more time to decide.

#### Does a PCT application extend the 20 year patent term?

No. In most countries the term runs from the international filing date. The PCT delays national examination, so it shortens the period during which a granted patent can be enforced.

#### Can a positive PCT search report speed up examination in India?

Not through the Global PPH, because India is not a member, and its PPH programme with Japan is limited. Applicants who chose the Indian Patent Office as ISA or IPEA can request expedited examination in the Indian national phase.

- Baker McKenzie note on the launch of ASPEC+

- FICPI report on the India and Japan PPH programme

- The Patents Act, 1970, published by IP India

## Patent Questions Founders Ask: US, Europe and India

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/patent-questions-founders-ask/

Founders in the US, UK and Europe ask the same patent questions again and again in online forums: what to file first, what it costs, whether software counts, and what happens if they have already launched. This page answers the most common ones in plain English.
The answers are written by PRASA IP's patent team, which includes in-house USPTO-registered and EPO-qualified patent attorneys and registered Indian patent agents. They are general information, not legal advice for your situation; patent rights depend on the facts, the dates and the countries involved.
Published 31 October 202612 minute read18 questions
On this page

- Filing strategy

- Cost and budget

- Software and AI

- Disclosure and timing

- Working with a firm outside your country

- Ownership and doing it yourself

### Filing strategy

#### Should I file a provisional application first?

Usually yes, if you need a filing date quickly and the product is still changing. A US provisional application secures a priority date for 12 months, and it costs far less than a full application. The catch: it only protects what it actually describes. A one-page sketch gives you a date for very little. Write it as close to a full specification as you can, with drawings and every variation you can think of.

#### Which country should I file in first?

Normally the country where the invention was made, and for most US founders that means the USPTO. The US and India both restrict filing abroad first. An invention made in the US needs a USPTO foreign filing licence before it is filed abroad, unless a US application was filed at least six months earlier. An Indian resident needs permission, or an Indian application filed at least six weeks earlier, under section 39 of the Patents Act. If inventors sit in both countries, plan the first filing before anyone files.

#### What is a PCT application, and do I need one?

A PCT application is a single international filing that keeps your options open in more than 150 countries. You file it within 12 months of your first application. It does not give you a worldwide patent: you still enter each country (the national phase) at around 30 or 31 months from your first filing date. Its value is time. You get roughly 18 more months to raise money and test the market before you pay for each country. Our guide on when to file a PCT application explains when it saves money.

#### Which countries should I protect in?

Pick the places where you sell, where competitors manufacture, and where an acquirer or licensee would care. For most technology startups that is the US first, then Europe through the EPO, then a short list such as the UK, China, Japan, Korea or India. Covering every country is rarely worth it. Covering the two or three markets that make up most of your revenue usually is.

### Cost and budget

#### How much does a patent really cost?

Official fees are the smaller part. Most of the cost is professional time: drafting the application, then answering the examiner's objections, often two or three rounds of them. A US patent taken from filing to grant typically runs into five figures in US dollars, and protection in several countries multiplies that. Spreading the spend over three to five years is normal, because each stage is paid when it falls due. See our patent filing cost comparison for India, the US and Europe.

#### Is there a cheaper way to do it?

Yes, without cutting quality where it matters:

- Use the fee discounts you qualify for. The USPTO cuts most fees by 60% for small entities and 80% for micro entities. In India, startups recognised by DPIIT pay reduced official fees and can ask for expedited examination.

- Spend on drafting, save elsewhere. A well-drafted first application avoids paying twice later. Searches, formalities and docketing can be done more efficiently.

- Use the PCT to delay costs while you find out which markets matter.

- Work with a team that has lower overheads. Firms like ours draft and prosecute from India, with US and European filings handled by our in-house USPTO-registered and EPO-qualified patent attorneys. The same work can cost much less than a large US or European firm charges.

More ideas are in our note on protecting IP on a startup budget.

#### Is a $199 provisional worth it?

Rarely. A provisional is only as good as its description. If it leaves out the features you later claim, those features get no benefit from the early date. A cheap filing can be worse than none, because it creates false confidence. Pay for a proper description, or at least have a patent professional review what you wrote before you file it.

### Software and AI

#### Can I patent software or an AI model?

Often yes, but not the code or the idea alone. Every major office asks what the software actually does technically:

- United States: claims must not be directed to an abstract idea. If they are, they need an inventive concept beyond it (the Alice test). Claims tied to a specific technical improvement, such as faster processing, less memory or better security, fare best.

- Europe (EPO) and the UK: a computer program “as such” is excluded. An invention that produces a further technical effect is patentable, though the UK applies its own test.

- India: section 3(k) excludes a “computer programme per se”. Inventions with a technical contribution, especially those tied to hardware or a technical process, can be patented.

For recent US practice, read our note on US patent eligibility declarations.

#### What about AI inventions specifically?

Protect the technical method, not the business outcome. Strong AI applications describe a specific training method, model architecture or data pipeline, and the measurable technical result it produces. An application that says “use machine learning to predict X” is weak everywhere. Also note: in the US, UK and Europe, a person must be named as inventor; an AI system cannot be. Our article on AI patent examination guidelines in India covers the Indian approach.

### Disclosure and timing

#### I already launched, demoed or published it. Can I still get a patent?

Possibly in the US, probably not in Europe. The rules differ by country:
| | Where | Grace period for your own disclosure
| United States | 12 months from your own public disclosure
| Europe (EPO) and UK | Effectively none; only narrow exceptions (abuse, certain official exhibitions)
| India | Limited to specific cases, such as notified exhibitions or papers read before a learned society

If you have disclosed, act fast and file in the US before the 12 months run out. Assume Europe is lost for whatever you showed, though later improvements can still be protected.

#### Does an NDA protect me if I show investors?

Yes, a confidential disclosure under an NDA is not a public disclosure. Many investors will not sign one, though. The safer order is to file first and pitch second. A provisional filed before the pitch gives you a date, and then you can talk freely.

#### How long does it take to get a patent granted?

Typically two to four years in the US and three to five at the EPO, depending on the technology. Most offices offer fast tracks. The USPTO has prioritised examination for an extra fee, and India offers expedited examination to startups and some other applicants.

### Working with a firm outside your country

#### Can a US, UK or European company use a patent firm based in India?

Yes, and many already do, for drafting, searches, prosecution support and patent analytics. What matters is who signs and files before each office. US filings and USPTO responses must come from a USPTO-registered practitioner. EPO work needs a professional representative before the EPO for non-European applicants. At PRASA IP those filings are handled by our in-house USPTO-registered and EPO-qualified patent attorneys. We also have in-house counsel for Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Africa and the UAE. You deal with one team instead of a chain of agents. See our international patent support.

#### Is the quality the same?

It depends on the people, not the postcode. Ask who will actually draft your application and what their technical background is. Ask for redacted samples of granted claims in your field, and how many rounds of examiner objections their applications usually need. A good firm answers all three without hesitation. Our guide to choosing an intellectual property lawyer explains how to check a professional's registration.

#### Is my invention safe if I send it abroad?

Use the same safeguards you would at home: an engagement letter with confidentiality terms and secure file transfer. Check export-control rules first. A US-made invention needs a foreign filing licence before it is sent abroad for filing, and some technologies (defence, encryption, dual-use) carry extra export restrictions.

### Ownership and doing it yourself

#### Can I file a patent myself?

You can file a provisional yourself, and some founders do. The risks come later. Claims and examiner responses decide what your patent actually covers, and that is where self-drafted applications usually go wrong. Middle ground: draft the technical description yourself, then pay a professional to review it and write the claims. Our step-by-step patent filing guide shows each stage.

#### My co-founder, contractor or university helped. Who owns the invention?

Whoever contributed to the claimed invention is an inventor. Ownership follows the contracts: an employment agreement, a contractor agreement or a written assignment. Without a signed assignment, a contractor can keep rights in what they invented, even if you paid for it. Get assignments signed before you file. Investors check this in due diligence, and gaps are expensive to fix later.

#### Do patents help with fundraising?

They can. A filed application shows investors you own something defensible, and it gives a buyer something to acquire. Investors look at quality more than numbers: one well-drafted application covering your core product counts for more than five thin ones.
Have a question that is not here? Send it to our patent team and we will tell you what applies to your invention and your markets.

### Official sources

- USPTO MPEP 140: foreign filing licences

- The Patents Act, 1970, section 39

- USPTO fee schedule

- WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty resources

### Related articles

- Startup IP on a budget. What to patent first

- How to file a patent in India, step by step

- Enablement of method of treatment claims after Teva v Lilly

## Software and AI Patents in India (Section 3(k))

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/software-ai-patents-india/

PRASA IP drafts and prosecutes patent applications for software, AI and machine learning inventions in India, the US and through the PCT. We are a Bengaluru firm in JP Nagar, led by two registered Indian patent agents who are also advocates: Praneetha K Rasbag and Sanath V Madgula.

### At a glance

- What we handle: AI and machine learning, data processing, networking and telecom, cybersecurity, embedded and IoT systems, fintech platforms, medical software and semiconductor design tools.

- Where we file: India, the United States (through PRASA IP LLC), and other countries through the PCT and foreign associates.

- Work we do: invention capture, patentability searches, drafting, responses to First Examination Reports, hearings before the Controller, and US and European filing strategy.

- How to reach us: online appointments or a meeting at our JP Nagar office in Bengaluru. Call +91 91132 14395.

### Can software be patented in India?

Yes, in many cases. Section 3(k) of the Patents Act, 1970 says that "a mathematical or business method or a computer programme per se or algorithms" are not inventions. The important words are per se. Indian courts have held that a computer-implemented invention is not excluded just because it runs as software. What matters is whether it makes a technical contribution or has a technical effect.

- Ferid Allani v Union of India (Delhi High Court, 2019) confirmed that inventions based on computer programs can be patented if they show a technical effect or technical contribution.

- Later Delhi High Court decisions, including Microsoft Technology Licensing v Assistant Controller, Raytheon v Controller General, OpenTV v Controller and Blackberry v Assistant Controller, have refined how "algorithm", "per se" and "business method" are read.

- The Patent Office's 2025 Guidelines for Examination of Computer Related Inventions draw on these cases. They give examiners a non-exhaustive list of technical effects, such as faster processing, reduced memory access time, improved signal transmission, better control of a machine, stronger network security and improved image or signal processing.

### What the Patent Office looks for

- A technical problem. What limitation existed in the earlier system: speed, accuracy, resource use, security, reliability or control of hardware?

- A technical solution. Which data structure, processing step, model architecture, training method or system interaction solves it?

- A technical effect you can show. Measured improvements, comparisons or worked examples make the effect easier to argue.

- A claim that recites the mechanism. Claims that only describe collecting data, running a model and producing a result are more likely to be treated as an algorithm or business method.

### AI and machine learning inventions

For AI inventions the specification must also be detailed enough for a skilled person to carry out the invention. The 2025 Guidelines follow the Madras High Court's approach in Caleb Suresh Motupalli v Controller of Patents on sufficiency of disclosure. In practice, describe:

- the model type and architecture, and why it was chosen;

- the training data, how it is prepared and labelled, and the features used;

- the training process and how the model is validated;

- how the model's output controls or improves a technical system.

We cover how examiners themselves may use AI in our note on India's AI guidelines for patent examination, and US eligibility in Recentive v Fox.

### Drafting for India, the US and Europe together

Most software clients file in more than one country. One specification can serve all of them if it is written for the strictest reader from the start.

- India: technical effect and contribution, read with Section 3(k) and the CRI Guidelines.

- United States: eligibility under 35 U.S.C. § 101, where a claimed improvement to computer technology matters.

- Europe: technical character and inventive step assessed on the features that contribute to a technical solution.

We draft method, system and, where useful, storage-medium claims, with dependent claims that hold real fallback positions. See when to file a PCT application for timing.

### Answering a First Examination Report

Section 3(k) objections are common for software applications. A good response:

- identifies the technical problem and effect from the original specification, without adding new matter;

- amends the claims to recite the technical features that produce the effect;

- relies on the relevant court decisions and the CRI Guidelines where they fit the facts;

- is filed within the 6 month deadline (extendable by 3 months), with a hearing requested if needed.

### How our fees are structured

- By stage. Patentability search, invention capture, drafting, filing, examination responses and hearings are quoted separately, in writing, before work starts.

- Official fees at cost. Government fees follow the IP India schedule and are lower for individuals, startups and small entities.

- Foreign filings. US, European and PCT costs are estimated as a programme so you can plan around funding.

### Common questions

#### Is software patentable in India?

Software that shows a technical effect or technical contribution can be patented. A computer program per se, a pure algorithm, a mathematical method or a business method cannot.

#### Can I patent an AI model in India?

A model that solves a technical problem in a technical way may be patentable, if the application discloses enough detail for a skilled person to reproduce it. A model described only by its business result is unlikely to be granted.

#### Should I file in India or the US first?

It depends on where you will sell, raise money and enforce. Indian residents generally need a foreign filing permit, or must file in India first, before filing abroad. We plan the order with you.

#### Do I need to visit your office?

No. Most software clients work with us online. You are welcome to meet us at our JP Nagar office in Bengaluru.

### Talk to our team

Send us a short description of the problem your software solves and how it works. We will tell you whether a patent is realistic before you spend on drafting. Call +91 91132 14395 or use the contact details on our home page.

Discuss a software invention
