## Types of Intellectual Property: India, US and EU

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/types-of-intellectual-property-protection/

By Praneetha K RasbagUpdated 23 October 202610 minute read
Intellectual property is a family of separate rights. Each one protects a different kind of creation, arises in a different way and lasts for a different time. Choosing the right one starts with knowing what each right actually covers.
In the United States the common shorthand is the four types of intellectual property. These are patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets. Indian law recognises those four and adds several specialised rights, including industrial designs, geographical indications, semiconductor layout designs and plant varieties. This guide explains each type under Indian law and notes how the same right works in the United States and the European Union.
The main types of intellectual property at a glance
- Patents protect technical inventions. Granted after examination. 20 years in India.

- Trade marks protect brand names, logos and other signs. Registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely.

- Copyright protects software, writing, art, music and films. Arises automatically. Generally life of the author plus 60 years in India.

- Industrial designs protect how a product looks. Registered. 10 years, extendable once by 5 years.

- Trade secrets protect confidential information. No registration. Lasts while the information stays secret.

- Geographical indications protect goods linked to a place, such as Darjeeling tea. Registered. 10 years, renewable.

- Semiconductor layout-designs protect integrated circuit layouts. Registered. 10 years.

- Plant varieties protect new plant varieties. Registered. 15 years, or 18 years for trees and vines.

### What are intellectual property rights?

Intellectual property rights, often shortened to IPR, are legal rights over creations of the mind. They cover inventions, brands, creative works, designs and valuable confidential information. Each right lets its owner stop others from using the protected subject matter without permission, within the limits the law sets.
Three features are common to almost every intellectual property right. The right is exclusive, so the owner decides who may use it. It is territorial, so a right granted in India does not by itself apply in the United States or Europe. Most rights are also limited in time. Patents, designs and copyright expire, while trade marks can be renewed indefinitely and trade secrets last while they stay confidential.
The WTO Agreement on Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights, known as TRIPS, sets minimum standards that member countries must provide. India, the United States and the EU member states are all WTO members, which is why the main rights look broadly similar across these jurisdictions even though the details differ.

### Patents. Protection for inventions

A patent protects a technical invention, such as a product, process, machine or composition, that is new, inventive and industrially applicable. It gives the owner the right to stop others from making, using, selling or importing the claimed invention in the country that granted it.

- India. Governed by the Patents Act, 1970. A patent must be applied for, examined and granted. The term is 20 years from the filing date. Section 3 excludes certain subject matter, including computer programmes per se, business methods and mathematical methods.

- United States. Utility patents last 20 years from filing. Design patents protect ornamental designs and, for applications filed on or after 13 May 2015, last 15 years from grant. Plant patents cover new asexually reproduced plant varieties.

- Europe. A European patent is granted centrally by the European Patent Office and then takes effect country by country. Since 1 June 2023 a Unitary Patent can also be registered, covering participating EU states under one right enforced before the Unified Patent Court.

### Trade marks. Protection for brands

A trade mark is a sign that tells customers who stands behind goods or services. It can be a word, logo, shape, colour combination or sound. Its job is to indicate origin, so a mark that merely describes the product is hard to protect.

- India. Governed by the Trade Marks Act, 1999. Registration lasts ten years and can be renewed indefinitely for further ten year periods. Unregistered marks are protected through the common law action of passing off, which depends on proving goodwill.

- United States. Rights arise from use in commerce. Federal registration with the USPTO under the Lanham Act adds nationwide notice and procedural advantages. Registrations are renewed every ten years, with a declaration of continued use due between the fifth and sixth years.

- Europe. An EU trade mark filed with the EUIPO covers all EU member states in one registration and lasts ten years, renewable. National marks remain available in each country.

### Copyright. Protection for creative and software works

Copyright protects original literary, artistic, musical and dramatic works, films, sound recordings and computer software. It protects the expression of an idea, not the idea itself. Copyright arises automatically when the work is created.

- India. Governed by the Copyright Act, 1957. Registration with the Copyright Office is optional but gives useful evidence of ownership. For most literary, artistic, musical and dramatic works, the term is the life of the author plus 60 years.

- United States. The term is generally the life of the author plus 70 years. Registration is optional for protection. For United States works, registration, or a refusal by the Copyright Office, is required before suing for infringement.

- Europe. Terms are harmonised at the life of the author plus 70 years for most works. There is no EU wide registration system.

### Industrial designs. Protection for appearance

A registered design protects the visual appearance of a product, such as its shape, pattern, ornamentation or configuration. It does not protect how the product works. Function belongs to patents.

- India. Governed by the Designs Act, 2000. The design must be new or original and must not have been published before filing. Protection lasts ten years and can be extended once by five years.

- United States. Product appearance is protected through design patents, described above.

- Europe. A registered EU design lasts up to 25 years in five year terms. An unregistered EU design gives three years of protection against copying from the date the design is first made available in the EU. Since 1 May 2025 the former Community design is called the EU design.

### Trade secrets. Protection for confidential know how

A trade secret is commercially valuable information that is kept confidential through reasonable measures. Recipes, source code, customer lists, manufacturing parameters and pricing models are common examples. Protection lasts as long as the secret is kept, and it is lost once the information becomes public.

- India. There is no dedicated trade secrets statute. Protection comes from contracts such as confidentiality and employment agreements and from the equitable law of breach of confidence. The Law Commission of India recommended a specific law in its 289th Report in 2024.

- United States. The Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016 created a federal civil action. Most states have also adopted the Uniform Trade Secrets Act.

- Europe. The Trade Secrets Directive (EU) 2016/943 sets common rules for unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure across member states.

### Rights that are specific to certain goods and technologies

#### Geographical indications

A geographical indication identifies goods as coming from a particular place where a quality or reputation is linked to that origin. Darjeeling tea and Mysore silk are registered Indian examples. The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 governs registration, which lasts ten years and is renewable.

#### Semiconductor integrated circuit layout designs

The Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Act, 2000 protects original layout designs of integrated circuits. Protection lasts ten years from the filing date or the date of first commercial exploitation anywhere, whichever is earlier. The register is little used, but it matters for chip design companies with Indian operations.

#### Plant varieties

The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 protects new plant varieties. Protection lasts 18 years for trees and vines and 15 years for other crops. The Act also preserves specific rights for farmers.
Which right fits the asset?
- A new technical feature or process points to a patent.

- A product name, logo or brand identity points to a trade mark.

- Software code, content, artwork or text points to copyright.

- A distinctive product shape or pattern points to a registered design.

- Valuable information that competitors cannot see points to trade secret protection.

- Most products need several rights at once. A consumer device can involve patents, a design, a brand and copyright in its software.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What are the four types of intellectual property?

The usual list is patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets. It is a convenient summary rather than a legal definition. India and the EU also protect designs, geographical indications and other specialised rights.

#### What is the meaning of IPR?

IPR stands for intellectual property rights. The term covers the legal rights that protect inventions, brands, creative works, designs and confidential business information.

#### Which intellectual property rights must be registered in India?

Patents, registered designs, geographical indications, layout designs and plant variety rights exist only through registration. Copyright arises automatically. Trade marks can be protected without registration through passing off, but registration makes enforcement far simpler.

#### Can one product be protected by more than one right?

Yes. A smartphone can carry thousands of patents, registered designs for its shape, trade marks for its name and logo, and copyright in its software. The rights overlap because they protect different aspects of the same product.

#### How many types of intellectual property rights are there in India?

Indian law protects eight main types: patents, trade marks, copyright, industrial designs, geographical indications, semiconductor integrated circuit layout-designs, plant varieties and trade secrets. Each has its own statute except trade secrets, which are protected through contracts and the law of confidence. Lists of four, five or seven types are summaries that group or leave out some of these.

#### What are some examples of intellectual property?

A patented battery chemistry, the name and logo of a product, the source code of an app, the shape of a bottle, a customer list kept confidential, and Darjeeling tea as a geographical indication are all examples. One product often involves several of them at once.

#### What is the difference between IP and IPR?

IP, intellectual property, is the creation itself, such as an invention, a brand or a piece of software. IPR, intellectual property rights, are the legal rights that let the owner control how that creation is used. In everyday use the two terms are often used interchangeably. Which professional you need depends on the right involved; our guide to choosing an intellectual property lawyer explains when you need a patent agent, a trade mark agent or an advocate.

#### Does Indian protection extend to other countries?

No. Intellectual property rights are territorial. International treaties such as the Paris Convention, the PCT, the Madrid Protocol and the Hague Agreement simplify filing abroad, but protection still arises country by country or region by region.

### Official sources

- The Patents Act, 1970, published by IP India

- The Trade Marks Act, 1999, published by IP India

- WTO overview of the TRIPS Agreement

- USPTO overview of patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets

- European Patent Office guide to the Unitary Patent

- EUIPO guide to EU designs

- European Commission IP Helpdesk note on the proposed Indian trade secrets bill

- Can you reuse IP India data and judgments?

## Design Registration in India: Process, Fees, Term

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/industrial-design-registration-in-india/

Updated 6 November 20268 minute readBy Sanath V Madgula, reviewed by Praneetha K Rasbag, Advocate
Talk to us about your designCall +91 91132 14395, message us on WhatsApp or email contact@prasaip.com. Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 6:30 pm IST. You can also book a call online.

PRASA IP helps product companies, hardware startups and manufacturers in Bengaluru and across India register designs and enforce them. A design registration is often the quickest and least expensive way to stop copies of a product's look.
Design registration in India at a glance
- Law: the Designs Act, 2000 and the Designs Rules, 2001.

- What it protects: the visual appearance of an article, judged by the eye. Not how it works.

- Application: Form 1, filed online with the Design Office.

- Official filing fee: ₹1,000 for an individual, startup or small entity, ₹4,000 for other applicants.

- Term: 10 years, extendable once by 5 years, so 15 years in total.

- Priority: file in India within 6 months of a first filing abroad to claim its date.

- Classification: the Locarno International Classification.

### What a design registration protects

Under the Designs Act, 2000, a design is the visual appearance of an article, judged by the eye. It must be:

- New or original, and not published or used anywhere in the world before the filing or priority date.

- Significantly distinguishable from known designs or combinations of known designs.

- Applied to an article by an industrial process, whether manual, mechanical or chemical.

A design registration does not protect how a product works. Functional or mechanical features need a patent, and brand names and logos need a trade mark. Many products need more than one. Our overview of the types of intellectual property explains which right covers what.

### Screen designs, GUIs and icons

Graphical user interfaces and icons were refused inconsistently for years. In March 2026 the Calcutta High Court held that there is no blanket exclusion for GUIs, and the Designs Office has since published draft guidelines on how it will examine them. Our article on GUI and icon design registration in India explains what the draft says and what it leaves open.

### Before you file

- Keep it confidential. Showing the design publicly, at a launch, online or to buyers without a confidentiality agreement, can destroy novelty. Exhibition at a notified exhibition has a limited grace period, so check before relying on it.

- Search earlier designs. We search the Indian design register and other sources to see whether similar designs already exist.

- Choose the class. India follows the Locarno International Classification, and the application must name the class and the article.

- Prepare the views. Clear drawings or photographs from each relevant angle define the scope of protection, so they matter as much as the application form.

### Forms and official fees

| | Step | Form | Individual, startup or small entity | Other applicants
| Application for registration | Form 1 | ₹1,000 | ₹4,000
| Claim startup or small entity status | Form 24 | Filed with the application, with proof of status
| Extension for a further 5 years | Form 3 | ₹2,000 | ₹8,000
| Restoration of a lapsed design, within 1 year of lapse, plus the extension fee | Form 4 | ₹1,000 | ₹4,000

To pay the lower fees, a startup must hold DPIIT recognition under the Startup India scheme and a small entity must have Udyam registration. The extension must be filed before the first 10 years end. Search, preparation of the representations and professional fees are extra.

### The registration process in India

- Filing. We file the application with the representations, the statement of novelty and any disclaimer at the Design Office, part of the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks.

- Examination. An examiner checks the application against the Act and may raise objections.

- Response. We answer objections in writing and, if needed, at a hearing. The application must be put in order for acceptance within the period set by the Designs Rules.

- Registration and publication. Once accepted, the design is registered and published in the official journal, and a certificate is issued.

Registration takes effect from the date of filing, or the priority date for a convention application. If you have already filed abroad, an Indian application claiming priority must be made within 6 months of the first filing.

### How long protection lasts

A registered design is protected for 10 years. It can be extended once, by 5 years, if the extension fee is paid before the first term ends, giving 15 years in total. We track renewal dates for our clients.

### Enforcing a registered design

Copying a registered design, or an obvious imitation of it, on the same class of article is piracy under the Designs Act. Remedies include an injunction and damages through the courts. A registered design can also be challenged by a cancellation petition, so a careful search and accurate filing make the registration stronger. Our note on the eye test in design infringement shows how courts compare designs.

### Common questions

#### How much does design registration cost in India?

The official fee for a design application on Form 1 is ₹1,000 for an individual, startup or small entity and ₹4,000 for other applicants. Search, drawings and professional fees are extra.

#### How long does a registered design last in India?

10 years, extendable once by 5 years, so 15 years in total. The extension must be filed on Form 3 before the first 10 years end and costs ₹2,000 for an individual, startup or small entity and ₹8,000 for other applicants.

#### Can I register a design after launching the product?

Usually not. Once a design has been published or sold, it is generally no longer new. File before launch, or check the facts with us quickly if the design has already been shown.

#### Can one product have both a design and a patent?

Yes. A design covers the appearance and a patent covers the technical function. Hardware products often benefit from both.

#### Is a design registration the same as copyright?

No. Copyright in an artistic work used as a design for industrial production can be limited, so a registered design is usually the right protection for a mass-produced product's appearance.

#### Do I need to visit the office?

No. Filing is online and we work with clients across India by video call. You are welcome to meet us at our JP Nagar office in Bengaluru.

### What happens when you contact us

- Confidentiality first. We first need a confidentiality agreement in place. Please ask us and we will send one.

- Assessment and quote. We review the design and tell you which rights fit, in which countries, with the official and professional fees for each stage.

- Work begins. Once you approve the scope, the partner handling your matter starts the search, drawings and filing.

Our founders handle each matter directly. Praneetha K Rasbag is an Advocate and registered patent agent, and Sanath V Madgula is an Advocate and registered patent agent.

## How Long Does IP Last? Terms and Renewals

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/how-long-does-ip-protection-last/

By Praneetha K RasbagPublished 31 October 2026Updated 25 November 20267 minute read
A patent lasts 20 years, a trade mark 10 renewable years, an Indian design up to 15 years and Indian copyright life plus 60 years. In the US and the EU, copyright runs for life plus 70 years. Patents and trade marks stay alive only if renewal or maintenance fees are paid on time.
The details decide real value. When does the clock start? What keeps the right alive? Can the term be extended? This guide answers those questions for India, the United States and Europe, with notes on the UK and China where the rules differ.
Key points
- Patents last 20 years from the filing date in India, the US, at the EPO and in China. Renewal or maintenance fees must be paid to keep them in force.

- India has no patent term adjustment for office delay. The US and China do. The Supreme Court of India is now examining the question.

- Trade marks are registered for 10 years at a time in India, the US and the EU. They can be renewed without limit.

- Registered designs last up to 15 years in India and the US, and up to 25 years in the EU and the UK.

- Copyright lasts for the author's life plus 60 years in India, and life plus 70 years in the US and the EU.

### Patents: 20 years from filing, if you pay to keep them

#### India

Section 53 of the Patents Act, 1970 sets the term at 20 years from the date of filing of the application. For a PCT application entering India, the term runs from the international filing date. Where a complete specification follows a provisional one, the 20 years run from the date the provisional was filed. So in India the provisional starts the clock.
The patent ceases to have effect if a renewal fee is not paid within the prescribed period. Section 60 allows an application to restore a lapsed patent within 18 months from the date it ceased to have effect. Restoration is not automatic.
India has no provision to add time when the Patent Office takes years to grant. A patent granted in year 8 still expires in year 20. The Supreme Court has agreed to examine this issue in Gunjan Sinha v Union of India. Our note on patent term adjustment in India explains what is at stake.

#### United States

Under 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2), a utility patent ends 20 years from the US filing date. If the application claims the benefit of an earlier US or PCT application, the term runs from the earliest such filing. This differs from India. Claiming priority from a US provisional application does not start the clock.
Two mechanisms can add time. Patent term adjustment under section 154(b) adds days lost to USPTO delay, such as a patent issuing more than three years after filing. Patent term extension under section 156 restores part of the time lost to regulatory review of a drug or similar product. That extension cannot exceed five years, and the remaining term after approval cannot exceed 14 years in total.
US utility patents carry three maintenance fees, due 3.5, 7.5 and 11.5 years after grant. A six month grace period with a surcharge follows each due date. Design patents work differently. For applications filed since 13 May 2015, they last 15 years from grant under section 173. They carry no maintenance fees.

#### Europe

Article 63(1) of the European Patent Convention sets the term of a European patent at 20 years from the date of filing. Article 63(2) lets member states extend protection for products that need marketing authorisation. In the EU this is done through supplementary protection certificates under Regulation (EC) No 469/2009. A certificate can last up to five years, plus six months where the paediatric rules apply.
Renewal fees for a European application are paid to the EPO from the third year. Under Article 86(2), that obligation ends with the fee for the year in which the grant is published. After grant, renewal fees are paid in each country where the patent is validated. For a European patent with unitary effect, they are paid to the EPO.

#### China

Article 42 of the Chinese Patent Law gives invention patents 20 years, utility models 10 years and designs 15 years, all from the filing date. Since the 2020 amendment, China compensates for unreasonable delay where an invention patent is granted more than four years after filing and three years after the request for examination. New drug patents can also receive up to five years of extra term, capped at 14 years of effective term after approval.

### Trade marks: 10 years at a time, renewable without limit

A trade mark can last indefinitely if it is renewed, and in some countries used.

- India. Section 25 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 registers a mark for 10 years. It can be renewed for further periods of 10 years. If a mark is removed for failure to pay the renewal fee, the Registrar may restore it on an application made after six months and within one year from expiry.

- United States. A registration lasts 10 years under 15 U.S.C. 1058. The owner must also file a declaration of use between the fifth and sixth years after registration, and again with each 10 year renewal. Without it the registration is cancelled.

- European Union. Under Article 52 of Regulation (EU) 2017/1001, an EU trade mark is registered for 10 years from the filing date. Under Article 53, renewal is requested in the six months before expiry.

The practical difference is the US use requirement. An Indian or EU registration can be renewed without filing proof of use at renewal. A US registration cannot. See our trade mark services page for how registrations work in each system.

### Designs: 15 years in India and the US, 25 in Europe

Design protection shows the widest gap between the major systems.

- India. Section 11 of the Designs Act, 2000 gives 10 years from registration. One extension of five years is available, for a maximum of 15 years.

- United States. A design patent filed since 13 May 2015 lasts 15 years from grant, with no maintenance fees.

- European Union. The design reform, Regulation (EU) 2024/2822, restated the term of a registered EU design. It lasts five years from filing and can be renewed in five year periods up to 25 years. Our note on the EUIPO trade mark and design changes covers the wider reform.

- United Kingdom. Section 8 of the Registered Designs Act 1949 gives five years at first, with four further periods of five years. The maximum is 25 years.

- China. Designs last 15 years from filing.

For a product with a long market life, such as furniture or an appliance, the extra decade in Europe matters.

### Copyright: life plus 60 or life plus 70

Copyright needs no registration in any of these systems. Its term depends on the author's life.

- India. Under section 22 of the Copyright Act, 1957, copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work published in the author's lifetime lasts until 60 years from the start of the calendar year after the author dies. A sound recording is protected for 60 years from the start of the calendar year after publication, under section 27.

- United States. Under 17 U.S.C. 302, copyright lasts for the author's life plus 70 years. A work made for hire lasts 95 years from first publication or 120 years from creation, whichever ends first.

- European Union. The Term Directive, 2006/116/EC, sets the author's life plus 70 years.

So a work may be free to use in India while it is still protected in the US and Europe.

### Other rights at a glance

- Plant varieties in India. Registration under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 lasts up to 18 years for trees and vines. Other crops get a shorter total term.

- Trade secrets. There is no registration and no fixed term. Protection lasts only while the information stays confidential.

Our guide to the types of intellectual property protection explains what each right covers.

### Practical steps

- Docket every renewal and maintenance date from the day you file. Most rights are lost through missed fees, not through litigation.

- For patents, count the 20 years from the filing date. Do not count from grant, except for US design patents.

- If a US patent took long to grant, check the patent term adjustment printed on it. For a pharmaceutical product, assess term extension in the US and supplementary protection in Europe early.

- Keep evidence of use for every US trade mark. You will need it in the sixth year and at each renewal.

- For a design with a long commercial life, consider European and UK filings, where protection can run to 25 years.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Which type of intellectual property protection has a set term of 20 years?

A patent. In India, the US, Europe and China, a patent for an invention lasts 20 years from the filing date, provided renewal or maintenance fees are paid. Some systems add time for office delay or regulatory approval.

#### How long does a patent last in India?

Twenty years from the date of filing, under section 53 of the Patents Act, 1970. For a PCT national phase application, the term runs from the international filing date. Renewal fees must be paid to keep the patent in force.

#### Does a trade mark ever expire?

Only if it is not renewed, or in some systems if it is not used. In India, the US and the EU, a registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed again and again.

#### When does intellectual property need to be renewed?

It depends on the right. An Indian patent ceases if a renewal fee is not paid within the prescribed period, under section 53(2) of the Patents Act, 1970. A trade mark is renewed every 10 years in India, the US and the EU. A US registration also needs a declaration of use between the fifth and sixth years. An Indian design gets one five year extension after the first 10 years. Copyright needs no renewal.

#### Can a lapsed IP right be restored?

Sometimes. In India, an application to restore a lapsed patent can be made within 18 months under section 60. A trade mark removed for non renewal can be restored on an application made after six months and within one year from expiry, under section 25.

## Startup IP on a Budget: What to Patent First

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/startup-ip-budget-patents-trademarks/

By Sanath V MadgulaPublished 29 September 20269 minute read
A large patent and trade mark portfolio can look impressive in a pitch deck. For an early startup it can also become a recurring bill that grows every year, in every country, whether or not the product survives.
Patents and trade marks are not one time costs. Each patent family carries drafting and filing fees, examination fees, attorney fees for every office action, and renewal fees that usually rise with age. Each country multiplies the bill. A startup that files widely in its first year can find that its IP budget competes with hiring and product work just when cash matters most. The answer is not to avoid IP. It is to file for what the business actually needs, in the order it needs it. The principles below apply whether the company is based in India, the United States or Europe, and the country notes show where the rules differ.

### Start with the business question, not the filing question

Before any application, ask what the company must stop competitors from doing in the next three to five years. The answer is usually narrower than the list of everything the engineers have built. A patent is worth its cost when it protects the feature that customers pay for, when copying would hurt the business, and when the company would realistically enforce it or license it.
Five questions before filing a patent
- Is the invention central to how the company earns revenue or raises money?

- Could you detect a competitor using it? Features inside a product are easier to police than server side processes.

- Will it still matter when the patent is granted, which often takes several years?

- Would you enforce it, license it or rely on it in a sale of the company?

- Could secrecy protect it better than publication in a patent?

If most answers are no, a patent is probably not the right spend yet. Good records, confidentiality and a clear ownership chain may protect the company better for a fraction of the cost.

### Do not disclose before you decide

Grace periods for an inventor's own disclosure differ sharply between major markets. The United States gives inventors one year from their own public disclosure to file. Japan also allows one year. Europe applies absolute novelty, with only narrow exceptions for evident abuse and certain officially recognised exhibitions. India's grace period covers only specified disclosures, and China's is similarly limited. A demo, investor deck on a public site or conference talk can therefore keep US rights alive while destroying European and Indian rights. If protection outside the United States may be needed, file before any public disclosure.

### Protect the brand first, but keep the filing narrow

A startup uses its name from the first day it trades. A clearance search before launch costs far less than a rebrand after an objection or a demand letter. File in the classes that cover what the company sells now and what it will sell soon. Filing in many classes for products that may never exist adds fees and can invite oppositions without adding real protection.

- India. Applications can be filed for marks proposed to be used, so there is no need to wait for sales.

- United States. An intent to use application reserves priority before launch. Registration follows only after the applicant proves use in commerce, and USPTO fees are charged per class.

- European Union. One EU trade mark covers all member states. The official fee for a second class is small, but each class from the third onwards costs noticeably more. The United Kingdom needs its own filing since Brexit.

- China. Trade mark rights go to the first filer. Startups that manufacture or source in China should file there early, before a supplier or distributor registers the brand.

The Paris Convention gives six months from the first trade mark filing to claim priority in other countries. Once the target markets are clear, one international application under the Madrid Protocol can extend a home application or registration to many member countries, including India, the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, China and Japan. Our trade mark services page explains the process.

### Stage patent spending so each step buys a decision

Patent procedure in the major offices lets a startup spend in stages and decide as it learns.

- Secure a cheap first filing. A US provisional application or an Indian provisional specification secures a filing date at a lower cost. There is no provisional application at the EPO, but a first filing in a European national office can serve the same purpose. The UK IPO, for example, gives a filing date to a description filed without claims or fees. Whatever the office, the first filing must describe the invention fully, because features left out do not get its date.

- Decide at month 12. The priority year ends 12 months after the first filing. By then, file the complete or non provisional application at home and decide whether protection abroad is worth pursuing. A PCT application keeps foreign options open for up to 30 or 31 months from the priority date.

- Enter only the markets that matter. Choose countries where the company sells, manufactures or expects to be copied. Every country added means years of fees and local attorney costs.

- Use a Unitary Patent where it fits. In Europe, a Unitary Patent covers the 18 EU states that have ratified the Unified Patent Court Agreement for one renewal fee. It is often cheaper than validating separately in four or more of those states. The United Kingdom, Spain, Switzerland and several others still need national validation.

Our guide on when to file a PCT application explains when that route saves money and when a direct filing is better. The Indian patent filing guide covers each Indian step and deadline. Our guide to choosing an intellectual property lawyer explains how to compare advisers and quotes.

### Check national security clearance before filing abroad

Several countries require permission before an invention made there is first filed abroad. The United States requires a foreign filing licence before an invention made there is filed abroad. It is usually granted in the filing receipt of a US application, and once six months have passed since the US filing no licence is needed unless a secrecy order was issued. India requires permission under section 39 of the Patents Act unless an Indian application was filed at least six weeks earlier. China requires a confidentiality examination for inventions completed in China, and breaching it can invalidate the Chinese patent. The United Kingdom has a similar rule for certain sensitive inventions. A distributed team with inventors in several countries should settle the filing sequence before anything is filed.

### Use every fee concession you qualify for

#### United States

The USPTO gives small entities a 60 per cent reduction and micro entities an 80 per cent reduction on many patent fees. Micro entity status has income and filing history limits, with a separate route linked to US universities. Eligibility must hold at every fee payment, so it should be checked and recorded carefully. Track One prioritised examination can bring a final decision within about a year for an additional fee, which is also reduced for small and micro entities.

#### Europe

Since 1 April 2024, the EPO has cut many fees by 30 per cent for micro enterprises, natural persons, non profit organisations, universities and public research organisations. It is available only if the applicant has filed fewer than five European applications in the five years before the application concerned. SMEs that are not micro enterprises do not qualify.

#### India

Startups recognised by DPIIT, natural persons, small entities and educational institutions pay reduced official patent fees. The Startup India portal describes the startup patent rebate as 80 per cent and the trade mark rebate as 50 per cent compared with other companies. Startups can also request expedited examination. The Start-ups Intellectual Property Protection scheme, known as SIPP, reimbursed the professional fees of empanelled facilitators. Published commentary reports that it ended on 31 March 2026, with no extension announced by mid 2026. The official fee concessions are separate and continue.

#### PCT

WIPO reduces certain PCT fees by 90 per cent for natural persons who are nationals and residents of listed countries, including India. The reduction does not apply to companies. The choice of International Searching Authority also changes the search fee considerably.

### Prune the portfolio every year

Renewal fees are where portfolios quietly drain cash. US maintenance fees fall due at three and a half, seven and a half and eleven and a half years after grant. A European application carries annual renewal fees at the EPO from the third year while it is pending, and after grant in each validated country, except in the participating EU states when a Unitary Patent is chosen. Indian renewal fees are payable every year and increase over the life of the patent.
Review the portfolio at least once a year. Ask whether each right still covers the product, still matters in that country and still supports a licence, a sale or investor diligence. Letting a weak right lapse is a sound business decision, not a failure.

### Low cost protection that every startup needs

- Written IP assignment clauses for founders, employees and contractors. Investors in every major market check ownership before they check patents. Some countries add their own rules, such as statutory compensation for employee inventors in Germany.

- Confidentiality agreements before sharing technical detail with partners, vendors or potential investors.

- Dated invention records, design files and code repositories that show who created what and when.

- Trade secret discipline for algorithms, data and processes that customers never see. The US Defend Trade Secrets Act and the EU Trade Secrets Directive both protect only information kept under reasonable secrecy measures. India relies on contract and the law of confidence.

- An open source policy, so that licence obligations do not undermine proprietary code.

Copyright in software code and content arises automatically in India, the United States and Europe. In the United States, registration is required before suing over a US work, and early registration improves the remedies available. Our overview of the types of intellectual property explains which right fits which asset.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Do investors expect a startup to have patents?

Not always. Investors in India, the United States and Europe look first for clean ownership of the technology and brand, a clearance search for the name and a sensible filing plan. A few well chosen applications usually impress more than a large, unfocused portfolio.

#### Should a startup file a patent before launching the product?

If the launch will disclose the invention and a patent may be needed outside the United States, file first. The US grace period does not protect rights in Europe, India or China.

#### How many trade mark classes should a startup file in?

File in the classes that cover the goods and services the company offers now or will offer soon. Add classes as the business expands.

### Official sources

- USPTO guidance on micro entity status

- USPTO prioritised examination FAQ

- EPO fee reductions for smaller applicants

- Unified Patent Court member states

- Startup India intellectual property benefits for recognised startups

- IP India patent forms and official fees

- WIPO note on the 90 per cent reduction in PCT fees

- Commentary on the end of the SIPP scheme by S.S. Rana and Co.

## Patent Filing in Bangalore: Agents and Attorneys

Source: https://www.prasaip.com/ip-law-firm-bengaluru/

Talk to us about your matterCall +91 91132 14395, message us on WhatsApp or email contact@prasaip.com. Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 6:30 pm IST. You can also book a call online.

### Patent filing in Bangalore: office, steps and official fees

Applicants in Karnataka file with the Patent Office, Chennai. Rule 4 of the Patents Rules, 2003 fixes the office by where the applicant resides, has a place of business, or where the invention originated. There is no Patent Office branch in Bengaluru, but filing, examination and hearings are online.

- Provisional application. Form 1 with a provisional specification on Form 2. The official fee online is ₹1,600 for an individual, startup, small entity or educational institution, and ₹8,000 for others.

- Complete specification. It must follow within 12 months of the provisional under section 9(1). There is no extra fee up to 30 pages and 10 claims.

- Examination. A separate request on Form 18 costs ₹4,000 or ₹20,000. Without it, the application is not examined.

- Who may file. An applicant may file in person or through a registered patent agent. You can check any agent on the IP India register of patent agents.

Professional fees for drafting and filing are separate from these official fees. Our guide to patent filing cost in India sets out the full fee schedule. Updated 24 November 2026.

### Patent agents and IP services in Bangalore

A filing is one step in an intellectual property strategy. The right starting point may be a patentability review, a trademark clearance search, a filing plan before public disclosure, or an assessment of an existing portfolio. Our team works with inventors, founders, in-house counsel, research groups and foreign associates to define the question first, then the appropriate work and jurisdiction.

PRASA IP is based in JP Nagar, Bengaluru (Bangalore). Our founders are registered Indian patent agents and IP attorneys, and they handle each matter directly. We assist clients in India and abroad: our team includes USPTO-registered and EPO-qualified patent attorneys and in-house counsel for Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Africa and the UAE. We do not assume that every invention needs a patent or that a filing alone answers a client's commercial risk.

### Patent lawyers for drafting, filing and prosecution

As a patent service provider for startups in Bangalore, we often prepare a filing plan before a product launch, a public demo or an investor pitch. We help founders decide between a provisional and a complete application and plan the costs of later filings.

Our patent lawyers are registered Indian patent agents with engineering backgrounds, so the person who discusses your invention also drafts and prosecutes it. Patent work begins with the technical disclosure. We discuss the inventive concept, implementation, alternatives, prior art and intended markets before deciding how to structure claims and a specification. ### Trademark search, registration and brand protection

A name chosen for a product or company should be assessed before it becomes difficult to change. Our trademark practice covers searches, identification of relevant goods and services, Indian applications, examination responses, hearings, opposition support, renewals and portfolio management. We distinguish a search for earlier marks from a broader clearance opinion, and a registry objection from an opposition by another rights holder. The advice and evidence needed differ for each stage. Our trade mark infringement examples show how disputes play out.

Inventions and brands are not the whole portfolio. ### Common questions

#### When should I consult a patent professional?

Ideally before a public demonstration, publication, sale or disclosure outside an appropriate confidentiality arrangement. Bring a technical description, drawings if available, the dates of any disclosures and a list of intended countries. The possible effect of disclosure depends on the jurisdiction and facts.

#### Can a Bengaluru firm support US or European patent matters?

Yes. We provide drafting, claim analysis, prosecution support and coordination. Representation before the USPTO and the EPO is handled by our in-house USPTO-registered and EPO-qualified patent attorneys.

#### Does a trademark application guarantee registration?

No. The Registry examines the application, and third parties may oppose it. A pre-filing search and carefully prepared application can help identify issues, but the outcome depends on the mark, goods or services, prior rights and evidence.

#### What happens at the first discussion?

We identify the subject matter, relevant deadlines, jurisdictions and the decision you need to make. Before receiving unpublished technical material, we can agree the engagement scope and a secure transfer method.

#### How do I choose the best patent agents in Bangalore?

Check that the agent is on the IP India register of patent agents, has a technical background close to your invention, and will draft and prosecute the application personally. Ask for a written, stage-by-stage quote. Our guide to choosing an IP lawyer lists the checks.

#### Where is a patent application from Bangalore filed?

Applicants in Karnataka file with the Chennai branch of the Indian Patent Office, and filing, examination and hearings are almost entirely online. Patent registration in Bangalore follows the same steps as anywhere in India; see our step-by-step patent filing guide.
